title: Redwood discovery - Harbor Payments latency & throughput
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets for real-time payments fraud flow, expected concurrency patterns, streaming requirements, and benchmark plan. Harbor Payments prefers predictable latency (p95 <= 120ms for short prompts, 500ms for 8k streams) but also needs cost controls; evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated with Private VPC option for compliance.
transcript:
00:00 Maya (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, happy to have Harbor Payments folks here. we scheduled 45 minutes, we'll run through your latency/throughput needs and figure out next steps. (muffled)
00:12 Liam (SRE): thanks, yeah we have tight deadlines; our fraud model has a p95 SLA requirement for the inline flow. currently using a mix of self-hosted and openai endpoints for research.
00:23 Carlos (SE): quick intro from me, i'm carlos from redwood infra team, i'll dig into perf and benchmarks. can you share your target p95 and concurrency?
00:32 Priya (ML): sure our critical path is real-time scoring for transactions, typical prompt lengths ~50-120 tokens, sometimes multi-turn context up to 2k. target p95 for the inline path is 120ms for short prompts, 400-600ms for up to 2k context. for batch/review flows we accept higher latency.
00:52 Maya: got it. and concurrency? how many parallel requests during peak?
01:00 Jamal (CTO): during peak we see ~600 rps for scoring, but that's spiky; sustained concurrency around 200-300. we need graceful degradation; can't drop below 70% throughput during incidents.
01:18 Carlos: ok that's helpful. two immediate architecture options: hosted redwood api (fast onboarding, auto-scaling) or dedicated pools (reserved gpu capacity, more predictable tail latency). private/vpc for compliance also possible. tradeoffs are cost vs predictability.
01:36 Liam: can hosted hit the p95 targets? tail latency is our worry — p95 spikes have killed us in the past with multi-tenant endpoints.
01:45 Carlos: depends on model and sequence length distribution — short prompts hit much lower kernel times. for hosted we have routing policies that route by latency SLO, but for strict p95 you often want dedicated capacity or pinned instances to avoid noisy neighbors. also warm KV cache for repeated prefixes helps.
02:05 Priya: we also stream responses for partial scoring (we need early tokens). how does streaming affect tokens/sec and p95?
02:14 Carlos: streaming adds overhead — initial token comes from first decode, so we measure time-to-first-token and time-per-token. for our benchmarks we report ttf (time to first token), p95 of ttf, and sustained tokens/sec. streaming can improve perceived latency if you can use partial results.
02:32 Maya: do you have example benchmark numbers for a 7B open model quantized on A100-like hardware?
02:40 Carlos: rough ballpark — single GPU q7b optimized on A100 variant: short (<=128 tokens) request p95 ~80-150ms with continuous batching disabled; with batching tuned you can get better throughput but may add a 10-50ms latency. tokens/sec depends on batch and kv cache; 7B can do ~1.5k-3k tokens/sec depending on kernel and hw. these are approximate.
03:05 Priya: our worst case is 8k context with streaming; p95 target there is more like 500ms to first token but we want stable per-token throughput after that.
03:17 Carlos: 8k context changes kernel selection; memory and kv-cache IO spikes. for long contexts, dedicated nodes with higher memory + quantization profile are recommended. also you can partial-eval prefix to reduce active sequence.
03:32 Liam: security/compliance: we need SOC2 in provider, KMS integration for keys, audit logs retained 1 year, and VPC/private option for production. can hosted do that?
03:45 Maya: hosted supports SOC2, we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments; hosted offers encryption at rest and in transit but for strict key control we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC. we can share SOC2 and security docs.
03:59 Jamal: ok next on benchmarking — we want a sample run: 1000 concurrent simulated requests with our token distribution (70% short prompts 50-150 tokens, 30% long 2k-8k). can you run that and provide p50/p95/p99?
04:16 Carlos: yes we can. typical steps: 1) Redwood SE configures dedicated bench cluster or hosted lane, 2) upload a representative prompt set or traffic replay, 3) run warmup to populate KV, 4) run multi-stage: ramp, sustain, spike. results include ttf, per-token throughput, GPU utilization.
04:36 Priya: who owns the infra for the dedicated bench? we need isolation and data not leaving our VPC.
04:42 Carlos: for private/dedicated we can run within your VPC or host a private bench with sample data sanitized. we have a hosted test too but for exact compliance we do bench inside your network.
04:53 Liam: any docs on model variants and quantization tradeoffs? our team worries about hallucinations when applying aggressive quantization.
04:59 Maya: yes we have a quantization guide and quality monitoring. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload and flags quality regressions in evals. we'll share the guide and an example eval run.
05:12 Jamal: pricing — how do you price dedicated? we need to compare unit costs vs hosted per-token.
05:19 Maya: dedicated is reserved capacity pricing (monthly/annual commit) with predictable throughput; hosted is usage-based per token. we'll send a pricing deck with examples for your workload.
05:29 Priya: on the benchmarks, can you measure streaming tokens/sec and time-to-first-token specifically? our SLAs mention early verdict within 150ms for fraud score.
05:36 Carlos: yes we'll include TTF and tokens/sec; we'll instrument traces to capture outliers and include per-token latency distribution. game plan: try hosted first for POC, but if p95 can't be met, propose dedicated pilot.
05:54 Liam: question on autoscaling: in a burst, how fast can dedicated scale? we have very bursty traffic at midnight closures.
06:02 Carlos: dedicated supports configurable autoscaling with burst capacity; scaling is constrained by model load times (model load can be minutes), so we recommend warm pools or overcommit to handle fast spikes.
06:15 Maya: for immediate POC we can allocate a small dedicated pool pinned to your model and run the benchmark. next steps: share traffic profile, we'll schedule benchmark, and send security/pricing docs.
06:28 Priya: sounds good. also, can you support single-tenant encrypted logs with 1-year retention?
06:33 Maya: yes on Private we can; on Hosted we have encryption and logs but customer-managed retention and single-tenant logs are Private/Dedicated addons.
06:44 Jamal: ok vendor risk — any notable competitors we should watch?
06:49 Maya: some teams compare to Anthropic and OpenAI for hosted APIs, and to self-host for cost control; for embeddings folks look at Pinecone for vector infra but that's complementary.
06:58 Liam: thanks. can you outline the benchmark timeline?
07:02 Carlos: propose: 1) by 2026-07-16 we get traffic sample and target p95, 2) by 2026-07-21 we run bench in reserved dedicated cluster, 3) share results within 48 hours of run, then decision on hosted vs dedicated pilot.
07:16 Priya: we'll also provide model artifacts for size estimation.
07:20 Maya: recap and owners: maya will send pricing and SOC2/security pack; carlos will set up the benchmark and coordinate with priya for traffic; priya to send sample dataset and p95 targets.
07:36 Jamal: cool thanks everyone.
07:40 (call ends)
next_steps: Maya send pricing deck + SOC2 and security docs (by 2026-07-16)
Carlos set up benchmark on dedicated cluster (target run 2026-07-21)
Priya provide traffic profile, sample prompts, and p95 targets (by 2026-07-16)
action_items: Carlos - configure dedicated benchmark and instrumentation - 2026-07-21
Priya - upload traffic profile and sample prompts - 2026-07-16
